package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions contain a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2019-7238) that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary system commands via a crafted HTTP request to a vulnerable REST API endpoint. This enables full compromise of the repository manager and its contents. While the package itself is not intentionally malicious, the vulnerability enables malicious exploitation with severe impact.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, upon receiving an HTTP request to a vulnerable REST API endpoint
execution_context.file_location: Core REST API handler class in the Nexus Repository Manager 3 server codebase (e.g., org.sonatype.nexus.repository.rest.*)
required_permissions: filesystem (to read/write files as the NXRM process)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the vulnerable REST API endpoint receives an HTTP request, the handler extracts a user-supplied parameter and passes it directly to a system command execution function (Runtime.getRuntime().exec), resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server with the privileges of the Nexus Repository Manager process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code directly executes user-supplied input as a system command without any validation or sanitization, which is a textbook example of a remote code execution vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal REST API handlers must never pass untrusted user input to system-level execution functions. Proper implementations validate, sanitize, or reject such input and restrict system command execution to authenticated, authorized, and tightly controlled contexts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System command execution may be legitimate in administrative modules or maintenance scripts, but only when strictly limited to authenticated users and with rigorous input validation to prevent injection.
key_indicators: Direct use of user input in system command execution functions (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec)
Absence of input validation or sanitization on parameters used in command execution
Exposure of system-level operations to unauthenticated or untrusted network requests
REST API handler code paths that invoke process execution based on HTTP parameters

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to the vulnerable REST API endpoint, supplying malicious input as a parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable handler processes the request and executes the supplied input as a system command.

attack_chain.action: The malicious system command runs with the privileges of the Nexus Repository Manager process, enabling the attacker to perform arbitrary actions on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the repository server, including data exfiltration, installation of webshells or backdoors, and potential lateral movement to other systems.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected system command execution (e.g., /bin/sh, cmd.exe) initiated by the Nexus Repository Manager process in response to HTTP requests
Unusual child processes spawned by the repository manager service, especially shortly after REST API activity
HTTP requests to REST API endpoints containing suspicious or shell metacharacter-laden parameters (e.g., ';', '|', '&&')
file_indicators: Modifications or unexpected changes to core REST API handler files (e.g., org/sonatype/nexus/repository/rest/*)
Presence of unauthorized binaries, scripts, or webshells in repository server directories (e.g., /opt/sonatype/nexus/ or installation path)
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with payloads targeting vulnerable REST endpoints, especially with command injection patterns
Outbound connections from the repository server to external or attacker-controlled hosts following suspicious API activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor process creation events for the Nexus Repository Manager service, flagging any child processes that are not part of normal operation. Analyze HTTP access logs for requests to REST API endpoints with suspicious parameters or command injection patterns. Deploy a web application firewall (WAF) with rules to detect and block command injection attempts. Regularly audit code and configuration for unsafe use of system command execution functions, and ensure all user input is strictly validated and sanitized.
